# The proposal

## Overview
Transparent Statistical Learning with R/Shiny proposes consolidating a functional MVP designed to facilitate the application of Discriminant Analysis through an integrated workflow that connects data preparation, statistical diagnostics, methodological selection, modeling, evaluation, and interpretation of results.

Funding will support the technical strengthening of the MVP over six months, with emphasis on stability, modularization, reproducibility, testing, statistical verification, visualizations, and interface, strengthening existing functionalities and improving the robustness, reproducibility, and reusability of the platform through statistical tools and procedures available in R. The funded work will be carried out in two three-month stages: stabilization and preparation, followed by strengthening and improvements. These activities will provide a stronger and more reusable R/Shiny platform for users applying Discriminant Analysis.

## Detail

### Minimum Viable Product

The current MVP is a functional application developed in R/Shiny that integrates the main stages of statistical analysis within an interactive environment. The platform was initially developed around Discriminant Analysis, which constitutes the methodological focus of the platform, and subsequently incorporated other supervised statistical modeling alternatives.

The application is currently organized into eight main tabs: Load Data, Exploratory Analysis, Missing Values, Categorical Variables, Models, Discriminant Analysis, Logistic Regression, and Help. The MVP interface is currently available in Spanish. The platform provides more comprehensive analyses for the following models due to the assumptions, diagnostic criteria, and statistical procedures involved in their application:
•	Discriminant Analysis: The platform evaluates multivariate normality, means, standard deviations, statistical tests, covariance matrices, and Wilks’ lambda. Based on these results, it provides diagnostic information and guidance for selecting between Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) and Quadratic Discriminant Analysis (QDA).
•	Logistic Regression: The platform supports binomial and multinomial models and includes model-fit and performance indicators, multicollinearity analysis using VIF, and the detection of potentially influential observations using Cook's distance.

For all available models, the platform generates results and evaluation elements that include confusion matrices, performance metrics, and ROC curves. Depending on the model, additional outputs are provided, such as coefficient matrices, rule tables, and visualizations including decision trees, variable importance, and analysis of potentially influential observations. The platform also allows users to copy generated tables and charts for use in reports and documentation.

Functional Requirements

FR01. Improve the interface and interaction flows: Optimize navigation, organization, and analysis configuration through the use of Shiny and bslib, promoting a clearer and more consistent user experience.
FR02. Improve visualizations: Enhance the presentation and interactivity of charts and results to facilitate their exploration and interpretation.
FR03. Strengthen existing models: improve modeling procedures, diagnostics, results, and visualizations while maintaining the statistical procedures available in R as their foundation.

Non-Functional Requirements

NFR01. Modularity and maintainability: Consolidate modular and reusable code, separating the user interface, processing, statistical analysis, and visualization to facilitate maintenance.
NFR02. Quality and testing: Implement automated testing in R to verify core functions and critical components and to detect regressions during further development.
NFR03. Statistical verification: Verify the results of tab 6 (Discriminant Analysis) using reference datasets, controlled cases, and independent calculations.
NFR04. Usability: Improve the organization, navigation, consistency, and clarity of the interface, facilitating the execution of analyses and interpretation of the results obtained.
NFR05. Reproducibility: Maintain an organized, version-controlled repository and manage dependencies through renv to facilitate consistent reproduction of the environment and analyses.

### Architecture

Transparent Statistical Learning with R/Shiny is developed as an interactive application in R/Shiny, where R serves as the processing and statistical analysis engine, while Shiny provides the web environment, user interface, and management of the application's interaction flows and reactivity. The current codebase includes separate functions for data processing, statistical procedures, and the generation of tables and visualizations. The project will consolidate this structure through greater separation between reusable functions and user interface logic, together with improvements to reactive workflows and reproducibility.

### Assumptions

The architecture based on R/Shiny will be maintained, using the current MVP as the foundation for the funded phase.
Statistical functionalities will primarily use existing packages and procedures in R, without developing new statistical algorithms.
Interface and visualization improvements will be prioritized according to their contribution to clarity, navigation, understanding, and interpretation of results.
Functionalities requiring research or technical evaluation will be analyzed and tested before their final incorporation.

### External dependencies

The project depends on the R/Shiny ecosystem and the packages required for the interface, statistical processing and analysis, visualizations, modeling, and testing, including Shiny, bslib, testthat, and shinytest2. Packages specifically required by the statistical procedures and models will be managed using renv, facilitating consistent reproduction of the environment and its versions.
